atoms.text: ReplicaSync copies new objects from a source bucket to a destination bucket in another region so that a second copy exists for disaster recovery. In this setup, the replication role ReplicaSyncRole and the destination bucket acme-orders-replica both belong to account 111122223333. Because access stays inside a single account, the grant is made only through the identity-based policy attached to the role. Attach a policy to ReplicaSyncRole that allows s3:ReplicateObject and s3:ReplicateTags on arn:aws:s3:::acme-orders-replica/*. Do not change the bucket policy of acme-orders-replica, because it needs no statement for this role. Confirm that the role's trust policy lets the ReplicaSync service assume it. Create a replication rule on the source bucket that applies to the prefix orders/ and names acme-orders-replica as the destination. Upload a test object under orders/ and verify that its replication status becomes COMPLETED and that the object and its tags appear in the destination bucket.

ReplicaSync copies new objects from a source bucket to a destination bucket in another region so that a second copy exists for disaster recovery. In this setup, the replication role ReplicaSyncRole belongs to account 111122223333, while the destination bucket acme-orders-replica is owned by account 444455556666. Because access crosses an account boundary, the bucket owner must grant it in the bucket policy. In account 444455556666, add a statement to the bucket policy of acme-orders-replica that names arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/ReplicaSyncRole as the principal and allows s3:ReplicateObject and s3:ReplicateTags on arn:aws:s3:::acme-orders-replica/*. The role's own account should carry a matching identity-based policy and a trust policy that lets the ReplicaSync service assume it. Create a replication rule on the source bucket that applies to the prefix orders/ and names acme-orders-replica as the destination. Upload a test object under orders/ and verify that its replication status becomes COMPLETED. Then confirm that the object and its tags appear in the destination bucket.

SnapVault writes a nightly database snapshot to a backup bucket so that the data can be restored after a failure. The SnapVault job runs under the role SnapVaultWriter in account 222233334444, and the target bucket acme-db-backups is in the same account. Access is therefore granted only by the identity-based policy attached to SnapVaultWriter. In that policy, allow s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::acme-db-backups/snapshots/*. Also allow s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads on arn:aws:s3:::acme-db-backups so that interrupted uploads can be cleaned up. Leave the bucket policy of acme-db-backups unchanged. Configure the job to upload each snapshot in 64 MiB parts to the snapshots/ prefix with a date-stamped key. After the first run, check that the snapshot object is listed under snapshots/ and that no incomplete multipart uploads remain.

SnapVault writes a nightly database snapshot to a backup bucket so that the data can be restored after a failure. The SnapVault job runs under the role SnapVaultWriter in account 222233334444, and the target bucket acme-db-backups is owned by account 555566667777. Because the bucket is in a different account, the bucket owner grants access through a bucket policy statement. In account 555566667777, add a statement naming arn:aws:iam::222233334444:role/SnapVaultWriter as the principal that allows s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::acme-db-backups/snapshots/*. In the same bucket policy, allow s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads on arn:aws:s3:::acme-db-backups so that interrupted uploads can be cleaned up. The role's account should also hold an identity-based policy that permits these actions. Configure the job to upload each snapshot in 64 MiB parts to the snapshots/ prefix with a date-stamped key. After the first run, check that the snapshot object is listed under snapshots/ and that no incomplete multipart uploads remain.

RestoreRelay reads backup objects during a disaster recovery drill and rebuilds a recovery environment from them. Its role, RestoreRelayReader, and the bucket dr-backups are both in account 333344445555. Access is granted solely by the role's identity-based policy, and the bucket policy is left as it is. Add a policy statement to RestoreRelayReader that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::dr-backups/restore-set/*. Add a second statement that allows s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::dr-backups with a condition limiting the s3:prefix to restore-set/. The role is read-only, so do not grant any write or delete action. In the RestoreRelay console, set the source location to s3://dr-backups/restore-set/ and start a restore job. When the job finishes, compare the object count in the recovery environment with the count listed under that prefix.

RestoreRelay reads backup objects during a disaster recovery drill and rebuilds a recovery environment from them. Its role, RestoreRelayReader, is in account 333344445555, and the bucket dr-backups is owned by account 666677778888. Access is granted by a statement the bucket owner adds to the bucket policy. In account 666677778888, add a statement naming arn:aws:iam::333344445555:role/RestoreRelayReader as the principal and allowing s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::dr-backups/restore-set/*. Add a second statement for the same principal that allows s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::dr-backups with a condition limiting the s3:prefix to restore-set/. The grant is read-only, so do not include any write or delete action. The role's own account should hold a matching identity-based policy for these read actions. In the RestoreRelay console, set the source location to s3://dr-backups/restore-set/ and start a restore job. When the job finishes, compare the object count in the recovery environment with the count listed under that prefix.

LogKeep copies application logs once a day into a backup bucket so that a durable copy survives the loss of the primary log store. The copy task assumes the role LogKeepCopier, and the destination bucket corp-log-archive is in the same account, 777788889999. The grant therefore comes only from the identity-based policy on the role. Attach a statement to LogKeepCopier that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::corp-log-archive/daily/*. Do not edit the bucket policy of corp-log-archive. Set the task to write one gzip-compressed object per source host under daily/YYYY-MM-DD/. Enable the task option that sends a SHA-256 checksum with each upload so the storage service rejects corrupted transfers. Run the task manually once and confirm that each host's object appears under the current date prefix with a matching checksum.

In account 888899990000, add a statement naming arn:aws:iam::777788889999:role/LogKeepCopier as the principal and allowing s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::corp-log-archive/daily/*. The role's account should also carry an identity-based policy that permits the same action on that resource. Set the task to write one gzip-compressed object per source host under daily/YYYY-MM-DD/. IntegrityScan verifies backup copies by reading each object and comparing its checksum with a recorded manifest. The scanner runs as the role IntegrityScanRole, and the bucket vault-backups is in the same account, 101010102020. Access is granted only by the role's identity-based policy. Allow s3:GetObject and s3:GetObjectAttributes on arn:aws:s3:::vault-backups/nightly/*, and allow s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::vault-backups. Do not modify the bucket policy. The scanner writes its report to a local output volume and never writes to the bucket. Set the scan target to the nightly/ prefix and schedule it to run at 03:00 UTC. After the first scan, open the report and confirm that every listed object has a status of MATCH or an explicit mismatch entry.

IntegrityScan verifies backup copies by reading each object and comparing its checksum with a recorded manifest. The scanner runs as the role IntegrityScanRole in account 101010102020, and the bucket vault-backups is owned by account 303030304040. Because access crosses accounts, the bucket owner grants it through the bucket policy. In account 303030304040, add a statement naming arn:aws:iam::101010102020:role/IntegrityScanRole as the principal that allows s3:GetObject and s3:GetObjectAttributes on arn:aws:s3:::vault-backups/nightly/*, plus s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::vault-backups. The role's account should hold a matching identity-based policy. The scanner writes its report to a local output volume and never writes to the bucket. Set the scan target to the nightly/ prefix and schedule it to run at 03:00 UTC. After the first scan, open the report and confirm that every listed object has a status of MATCH or an explicit mismatch entry.

VersionMirror replicates object versions and delete markers into a versioned backup bucket so that the backup copy reflects deletions in the source. Its role, VersionMirrorRole, and the destination bucket ledger-replica are both in account 505050506060. The grant is made only in the identity-based policy of the role. Allow s3:ReplicateObject, s3:ReplicateDelete, and s3:ReplicateTags on arn:aws:s3:::ledger-replica/*, and allow s3:GetBucketVersioning on arn:aws:s3:::ledger-replica. Leave the bucket policy of ledger-replica unchanged. Confirm that versioning is enabled on both the source and destination buckets before you create the rule. Create a replication rule for the whole source bucket with delete marker replication turned on. Delete a test object in the source and verify that a delete marker is created in the destination while earlier versions remain.

VersionMirror replicates object versions and delete markers into a versioned backup bucket so that the backup copy reflects deletions in the source. Its role, VersionMirrorRole, is in account 505050506060, and the destination bucket ledger-replica is owned by account 707070708080. The bucket owner grants access by adding a statement to the bucket policy. In account 707070708080, name arn:aws:iam::505050506060:role/VersionMirrorRole as the principal and allow s3:ReplicateObject, s3:ReplicateDelete, and s3:ReplicateTags on arn:aws:s3:::ledger-replica/*, plus s3:GetBucketVersioning on arn:aws:s3:::ledger-replica. The role's account should also have a matching identity-based policy. Confirm that versioning is enabled on both the source and destination buckets before you create the rule. Create a replication rule for the whole source bucket with delete marker replication turned on. Delete a test object in the source and verify that a delete marker is created in the destination while earlier versions remain.

EdgeBackup is an on-premises gateway that uploads incremental file backups to a bucket and reads a manifest to decide which files changed. The gateway authenticates as the IAM user edge-gw-user in account 909090901111, and the bucket branch-backups is in the same account. Access is granted only by an identity-based policy attached to the user. Allow s3:PutObject and s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::branch-backups/site-12/*, and allow s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::branch-backups with the prefix condition site-12/. Do not alter the bucket policy. Store the user's access key in the gateway's credential file with file mode 600. Point the gateway at the prefix site-12/ and run a first full backup. Then modify a file, run an incremental backup, and confirm that only the changed file and an updated manifest.json are written.

In account 121212123434, add a statement naming arn:aws:iam::909090901111:user/edge-gw-user as the principal that allows s3:PutObject and s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::branch-backups/site-12/*, plus s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::branch-backups with the prefix condition site-12/. The user's account should also attach a matching identity-based policy. Store the user's access key in the gateway's credential file with file mode 600. Point the gateway at the prefix site-12/ and run a first full backup. Then modify a file, run an incremental backup, and confirm that only the changed file and an updated manifest.json are written.

PruneKeeper removes backup objects that have passed their retention date so that the backup bucket does not grow without limit. It runs as the role PruneKeeperRole, and the bucket cold-backups is in the same account, 131313134545. Access is granted only through the role's identity-based policy. Allow s3:DeleteObject and s3:DeleteObjectVersion on arn:aws:s3:::cold-backups/expired/*, and allow s3:ListBucket and s3:ListBucketVersions on arn:aws:s3:::cold-backups. Make no change to the bucket policy. Set the retention period in PruneKeeper to 90 days and limit its scope to the expired/ prefix. Run the first job in dry-run mode and review the list of objects it would delete. After you disable dry-run, confirm that only objects older than 90 days under expired/ are removed.
